europe_now.title: Student Protests in France
europe_now.summary: Tens of thousands of students and high schoolers have rallied across France, leading to widespread demonstrations and clashes in Paris. Protesters are demanding government action amid growing youth frustration and economic anxiety.

sources.headline: Tens of thousands rally across France as high school protests gather strength

europe_now.title: Security Threat in Poland
europe_now.summary: A man has been officially charged with plotting an assassination attack against the Polish prime minister. The security incident highlights heightened tensions and threats facing national leadership in Central Europe.

sources.headline: Man charged with plotting attack on Polish PM

top_stories.title: Pope Leo Lung Surgery
top_stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has successfully undergone a surgical operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung. The Vatican confirmed the procedure following his recent lung cancer diagnosis.

sources.headline: Pope Leo has cancerous growth removed in lung operation
Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says

top_stories.title: Spanish Sovereignty in Ceuta
top_stories.summary: The King of Spain visited the enclave of Ceuta to emphasize that the territory's sovereignty and territorial integrity are non-negotiable. The royal visit comes amid regional tensions and migration pressures involving Morocco.

sources.headline: King of Spain in Ceuta: ‘Sovereignty and territorial integrity are not negotiable, and faced with any risk, our duty is their defense’

top_stories.title: US-Russia Diesel Deal Scrutiny
top_stories.summary: European leaders and US lawmakers have raised significant concerns regarding a newly announced diesel agreement between the United States and Russia. Critics warn that the arrangement could undermine existing sanctions and weaken Western leverage.
